Loyalty card provisioning vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume storeCard-style passes in Wallet cover storefront language. PKPass signing, retail APIs, and Connect actually separate pass behavior from product-page copy:

  • PKPass storeCard-style pass templates & signing — creating .pkpass bundles with storeCard pass type, retailer logos, barcodes, and pass update web services. Controls whether shoppers hold a loyalty card in Wallet — not App Store language. AppLocale does not perform this.
  • Retail POS & loyalty-program APIs — point-of-sale, loyalty-program, or retailer partner APIs that fetch points balance, assign membership tiers, and push rewards updates to Wallet. Listing copy may mention points and rewards frames; building retail integrations is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • PassKit & Add to Apple Wallet APIs — wiring Add Loyalty Cards to Wallet buttons and pass update handlers in SwiftUI or UIKit. Listing copy may mention loyalty card frames; building PassKit code is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Apple Wallet as host app — loyalty cards appear as cards inside Wallet alongside other credentials. Your listing may reference Wallet → Loyalty Cards; localizing the App Store row does not change Wallet.app UI strings.
  • Points and rewards push updates — balance changes, tier upgrades, and punch-card stamp notifications pushed to the loyalty card in Wallet. Listing copy describes buyer-visible points and rewards frames — not push notification engineering.
  • In-app loyalty card labels — runtime strings on pass faces, points rows, punch-card stamps, or membership tier badges inside Wallet. Listing rewrite does not cover String Catalog entries rendered after install.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of loyalty card features in the binary.

Working loyalty card integration and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. Loyalty Cards–specific listing copy — what translates differently

Coffee shop, grocery, and retail loyalty card listings use vocabulary general Wallet guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe store rewards and membership cards — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Loyalty Cards vs Add Loyalty Cards to Wallet vs 会员卡 vs 积分卡 vs 忠诚卡

US pages use "Loyalty Cards", "Add Loyalty Cards to Wallet", or "Your rewards card in Apple Wallet." China storefront copy often uses 会员卡 for membership and store-card frames, 积分卡 when your English frames emphasize points balance, and 忠诚卡 when your English source uses loyalty-program branding. Apple keeps Loyalty Cards as a product term where appropriate alongside Chinese phrasing on screenshot overlays. Do not use 登机牌 — that signals airline boarding pass marketing. Do not use 活动门票 — that signals event ticket entry.

Points balance & 会员积分

Gallery frames show points balance rows on the loyalty card face — "1,250 Points" or rewards balance callouts. Chinese buyers expect 会员积分 or 积分 on points rows — distinct from airline gate rows on the Boarding Pass guide and venue entry on the Event Tickets guide.

Punch card & 打卡集点

Coffee shop and café frames often show punch-card stamp progress — "Buy 9, get 1 free" or stamp-collection callouts. Chinese App Store copy uses 打卡集点 when your English frames show punch-card or stamp-card progress — not 登机口 from the Boarding Pass guide or 座位区 from the Event Tickets guide.

Membership tier & 储值卡

Retail apps show membership tier badges or stored-value balance on loyalty card screenshots — "Gold Member" or prepaid balance callouts. Chinese copy uses 储值卡 when your gallery shows stored-value frames, or tier vocabulary that matches your English claims — describing the buyer-visible frame your screenshots show, not retail backend engineering we do not deliver.

Scan or tap at register

Loyalty card frames may show barcode scan or NFC tap-at-register flows on the pass face. Chinese copy may reference scan-or-tap checkout context when your English source includes register redemption badges — describing pass-face marketing, not POS terminal engineering.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Loyalty Cards–relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 会员卡, 积分卡, 忠诚卡, and 会员积分 each signal different intent from 登机牌 boarding passes, 演出票 event tickets, or generic 钱包 keywords.

FAQ

Does issuing loyalty cards in Apple Wallet auto-fill my China App Store listing?

No. Provisioning PKPass storeCard-style credentials, push points-balance updates to Wallet, and Add Loyalty Cards to Wallet flows control runtime behavior inside the binary — they do not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. If zh-Hans name, subtitle, keywords, description, or screenshot caption fields are empty or still English, the China storefront falls back to en-US copy.

Which App Store Connect fields does AppLocale rewrite?

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese for listing fields you specify: app name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines such as Loyalty Cards, Add Loyalty Cards to Wallet, points balance, rewards, punch card, membership tier, 会员卡, 积分卡, 忠诚卡, 会员积分, 打卡集点, 储值卡, and Wallet 会员卡 — rewritten from your English originals.

Loyalty Cards listing copy covers store loyalty, rewards, punch, stamp, and membership cards only — PKPass storeCard-style retail passes, points balance rows, punch-card stamps, membership tiers, and Add Loyalty Cards to Wallet on gallery frames. Why do my Loyalty Cards screenshot captions still say Points and Rewards in English on China?

Screenshot overlay lines and caption fields are per localization in App Store Connect. If you never filled zh-Hans caption fields — or pasted English into the Chinese screenshot set — China buyers see Latin script on frames meant to signal 会员卡, 积分卡, or 忠诚卡 value.

会员卡 fits membership and store-card frames. 积分卡 fits points-balance and rewards frames. 忠诚卡 fits loyalty-program positioning. 登机牌 fits airline boarding passes on the Boarding Pass guide. 演出票 fits event tickets on the Event Tickets guide.
